newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Investor posts jump in 1996 profits.
newsitem.headline: Investor posts jump in 1996 profits.

text.p: Swedish investment company Investor AB, the key holding company in the Wallenberg family's financial empire, said on Thursday total return for its shareholders jumped 60 percent in 1996.
This compared to an average increase of only 43 percent on the Stockholm Stock Exchange.

Its pre-tax profit soared to 9.60 billion crowns ($1.3 billion) from 3.05 billion a year earlier while its net asset value rose to 78.88 billion crowns from 50.07 billion calculated on December 31. Per share its net asset value was 394 crowns versus 252.
Company President Claes Dahlback called 1996 one of the best years ever.
"For Investor, 1996 was a very good year, one of the best in our 80 year history," Dahlback said in the statement.
"During the past 10 years, the Investor share has yielded an average total return of 20 percent annually, compared with slightly more than 15 percent for the Stockholm Stock Exchange," Dahlback said.
Investor, whose largest holding by value is Swedish drug company AB Astra, said it would pay out a dividend of 10 crowns per share compared to nine crowns last year.

The result reflected a capital gain of 12.40 for sale of a 55 percent stake in truckmaker Scania, which it sold in an international public offering. Its proceeds from the sale totalled 18.8 billion crowns.
The company said in its results statement that industrial investments performed favourable in 1996, thanks to strong conditions on the Stockholm Stock Exchange.
"The favourable climate for share investments was mainly attributable to a sharp fall in interest rates and large flows of capital to the stock market," Investor said.

The earnings statement also showed a 3.48 billion crown cash injection for Saab Automobile AB, which Investor owns jointly with U.S. vehicle maker General Motors/Opel. Investor will provide 1.74 billion crowns of this.
"A total of 1.05 billion crowns was paid out during 1996 and the remaining 690 million crowns will be paid out in June 1997," Investor said.
It said it received dividends during the year rose to 1.80 billion crowns from 656 million. This included shares in property company Diligentia which it received through its holding in S-E-Banken.
Investor bought shares in Swedish pharmaceutical company Astra worth 136 million crowns and shares in IT company WM-Data totalling 254 million crowns.
Saab AB, the company's wholly-owned aerospace and defence group, deepened its operating losses to 1.40 billion crowns compared to a loss of 354 a year earlier.
The company said earlier on Thursday that it had lifted its stake in S-E-Banken to 5.83 percent from 2.49 percent.
